query: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization but a low coercive field, and reported single-phase fcc high-entropy alloys derived from it have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe in the reported magnetic measurements. What single intervention could overcome this coercivity limitation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted change relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative, the relevant compositional, structural, and measurement boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Alloying single‐phase fcc FeCoNi with ~3 at.% Al and subsequently aging to produce coherent L12 Ni3Al nanoprecipitates will increase the coercive field by domain‐wall pinning and enhanced magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
generation.material_initial_state: Single‐phase fcc Fe35Co35Ni30 alloy with Hc ≤100 Oe
generation.intervention: Add 3 at.% Al to FeCoNi and age at 550 °C for 10 h
generation.conditions: Alloys homogenized at 1200 °C, water‐quenched, aged at 550 °C ±10 °C for 10 h; grain size ~20 µm
generation.structural_mediator: 5–15 nm coherent L12 Ni3Al precipitates at ~5–8 vol%
generation.mechanism: Precipitates pin domain walls and introduce higher magnetocrystalline anisotropy
generation.predicted_outcome: Hc increase from ~50 Oe to ~300–500 Oe with minimal Ms loss
generation.baseline: Fe35Co35Ni30 alloy processed identically but without Al
generation.boundary: Al content 2–4 at.%; aging temperature 500–600 °C; aging time 5–20 h
generation.uncertainty: Moderate; precipitation behavior and anisotropy contribution in FeCoNi–Al are not fully characterized

falsification_experiment.design: Produce two alloys: Fe35Co35Ni30 and Fe35Co35Ni30Al3, homogenize at 1200 °C, quench, age at 550 °C for 10 h. Characterize microstructure and magnetic properties.
measurements: TEM precipitate size and volume fraction
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Al‐added alloy does not exhibit at least a 200 Oe increase in Hc over the no‐Al baseline, the hypothesis is falsified.
